title: Mbakhalou Saloum, Peanut Rice of the Saloum Islands
author: Lamine Faye
desc: Rice cooked in a sauce of onions, meat or fish, nététou, guedj, yet, dried Saloum shrimp and 200 g of peanut powder, then steamed under a cloth.
longDesc: Lamine Faye of Louma by Seggfaye presents mbakhalou saloum as the emblem of the Saloum islands, ‘where the groundnut meets the mangrove’. Onions and meat are fried, nététou goes into the hot oil, 200 g of peanut powder is slaked in warm water and added with the guedj and yeet, and the sauce simmers 30 minutes. The rice is then added to the sauce and cooked until the liquid is fully absorbed, and the pot is finished by steaming under a cloth. The fish version is closer to the coast and islands; the meat version is common inland.
ingredients: Salt and pepper — quantities not printed
steps: Fry the onions and the meat in oil. Add the nététou to the hot oil.
Slake the peanut powder in lukewarm water and add it to the pot with the guedj and yeet.
Add the tomato concentrate, vegetables and the dried shrimp. Simmer 30 minutes over medium heat, until the sauce begins to take body.
Add the rice to the sauce and cook until the liquid is fully absorbed.
Finish by steaming under a cloth: the rice finishes swelling in the steam.
Add chile purée to taste and serve.
chefTips: ‘Cook until absorption is complete’ is the cue for the rice; the water quantity is not printed.
‘The sauce must be rich and fragrant’ is the page’s taste cue before the rice goes in.
The cloth-steam finish is part of the dish — don’t skip it.
Guedj and yeet are bought, already fermented; no fermentation is performed.
commonMistakes: Adding the peanut powder dry to the hot oil.
Over-salting before tasting the dried seafood.
reheating: Steam gently with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Peanut powder and dried shrimp make this a protein-rich rice.
culturalNote: ‘Celui de ma terre natale, les Îles du Saloum’, writes Lamine Faye — the dish of the author’s own home islands. Neither page that prints it names an ethnic group; it is attributed to a region only and is not labelled Serer here.
sources: Source: seggfaye.com (Louma by Seggfaye), byline ‘Par Lamine Faye’, published 10 June 2026. Cross-read against guide.seggfaye.com, which has no byline and no date and fails the sourcing bar on its own — used only as a second reading of the figures. Quantities AGREE across the two readings: treat as two-pass on figures, with the caveat that the second reading cannot be cited. Yield: ‘6 personnes’. Preparation 30 min, cooking 1 h, total 1 h 30.
Cues in short fragments: ‘Laissez cuire jusqu’à absorption complète’; ‘étuvage sous torchon’; ‘La sauce doit être riche et parfumée’. The shorter second reading prints ‘Cuire jusqu’à absorption’.

REGIONAL ATTRIBUTION, short fragments in the author’s own voice: ‘Celui de ma terre natale, les Îles du Saloum’ and ‘là où l’arachide rencontre la mangrove’. The second reading calls it the emblematic dish of the Saloum islands. Neither reading names an ethnic group.
ABSENT, not estimated: tomato concentrate, vegetables, salt, pepper; the rice-to-water ratio; the chile purée (‘à volonté’).
